title: Efficient Open Modification Spectral Library Searching in High-Dimensional Space with Multi-Level-Cell Memory
problem: Open Modification Search (OMS) for mass spectrometry analysis encounters exponentially growing search scope. Existing OMS accelerators have limited parallelism and fail to scale effectively with increasing data volumes.
motivation: OMS enables discovery of modified peptides in mass spectrometry analysis, which is critical for proteomics research.
method: The approach uses multi-level-cell (MLC) RRAM memory to increase storage capacity by 3x. In-memory computing performs computations directly on the RRAM, eliminating data movement overhead. Hyperdimensional computing provides error-tolerant computation that handles up to 10% memory errors while delivering massive hardware parallelism. The design was validated on a fabricated MLC RRAM chip.
key_novelty: Combining MLC RRAM with hyperdimensional computing to enable error-tolerant in-memory Open Modification Search.
contributions: MLC RRAM design achieving 3x storage capacity increase
In-memory computing architecture for OMS achieving 77x speedup
Hyperdimensional computing framework tolerating up to 10% memory errors
2-3 orders of magnitude energy efficiency improvement over existing approaches
